content.thinking:
I'm planning the elephant model as a low-poly African bush elephant facing +Z, with proportions around 3.2m shoulder height and 6m length, and mapping out which builder, math, paint, and path utilities I'll need before writing the full file in one pass.

I'm sketching the geometry: the body as a tapered sweep with elliptical cross-sections, four legs as tapered rods with flat feet and small toenail details, and a head built from a scaled sphere with a forehead dome, all positioned relative to the body's rear-to-chest coordinates. I'm now working out the trunk as a curling sweep from the head down to a narrow tip near the ground, tapering its radius along the path.

For texture I'm planning a wrinkle pattern along the trunk using a sine function on the sweep parameter to alternate between base and darker tones, then moving on to the ears, which I'm building as extruded outlines oriented sideways relative to the head, flaring outward along the x-axis.

Working out the ear outline points and placement, I realize the ear risks getting buried inside the body's radius if placed too close to the head's x-position, so I need to adjust its x-offset to keep it visible outside the shoulder.

Now I'm sketching the tusk curves as a swept catmull-rom path with tapering ivory radii, root thicker than tip, curving outward and down before sweeping forward and up.

For eyes, I'm working out placement on the head sphere using a directional angle approach, picking an azimuth and elevation to aim the eye outward and slightly upward, then projecting that direction from the head center to approximate the surface position despite the head not being perfectly spherical.

For the tail, I'm sweeping a tapered cylinder downward and backward with a darker tufted cone cap at the tip. For body shading, I'm planning a paint function that layers a mottled gray base with darker dust tones on the lower legs, using a height threshold to blend in the brown coloring near the ground.

I'm adding a subtle wrinkle effect using a noise-modulated sine pattern along the body's z-axis, darkening spots where the pattern peaks, then placing small flattened sphere toenails at the front of each foot in an ivory-gray tone.

For the head, I'm sketching forehead domes, temple shapes, and blending the trunk base into the skull, then considering a chin capsule, brow ridge spheres, and shoulder details to round out the anatomy.

Checking height proportions: ear tops, body sweep peak, head top, and shoulder line all need to line up around y=3.1-3.3, with leg radius matching hip overlap at the base.

Adjusting the belly curve lower and defining a profile function that tapers the body's width and height along its length, using a catmull spline path for the torso shape and ensuring the hindquarters sit slightly lower. Writing leg rod code...

Still shaping the trunk curve...
